key_insight: Post-training, especially supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, can turn generative LLMs into much stronger ICD coders than prompting alone.
clinical_relevance: Better automated ICD coding could improve billing, epidemiology, and clinical decision support by increasing code recall and set prediction quality.
method: Compared discriminative baselines with generative LLM coders under a shared evaluation protocol.
Tested prompting, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (GRPO) for ICD coding.
Introduced PHI, a diagnostic curriculum designed to improve missed-code cases and macro-level performance.
evidence_signal: The study used a controlled empirical setup with common protocols and metrics, and reports that prompting-only evaluation underestimates LLM coding potential while SFT and GRPO improve performance.
watch_item: Results come from a specific experimental protocol, so real-world deployment may still face dataset shift, taxonomy complexity, and coding workflow integration challenges.
paper_title: Can Post-Training Turn LLMs into Good Medical Coders? An Empirical Study of Generative ICD Coding
